chunk_findings.detail: The check's name and the surrounding scenario assert a specific property: that a *live* (non-expired) lease held by delta causes epsilon's claim to be refused. The new `or "delta's lease ran out" in err` branch accepts the opposite state of the world — delta's lease has already expired and the refusal comes from the grace-period path. So under the exact interleaving the bug describes (xdist throttling pushes epsilon's claim past the 2 s TTL, so `err` contains "delta's lease ran out" and `code == 3`), the check now reports success for a run in which the lease was *not* live, i.e. the premise the scenario claims to exercise was never exercised. Concretely, a server regression that computes the live-lease deadline wrongly and reports a still-live delta lease as "ran out", refusing epsilon with code 3, would sail through this check (old assertion failed, new one passes), which defeats the regression test's purpose — the flake is silenced by widening the oracle rather than by making the lease outlive the claim (e.g. a longer TTL or an explicit separate grace-period scenario). The comment in the diff ("still a refusal by the live (grace) lease") does not hold: a lease past its TTL is not live.

chunk_findings.detail: The new body-printing guard is broader than the "nothing else was printed" guard directly above it. The first `if` deliberately suppresses the stderr reason when `out.exit in (NOTHING, REFUSED)` *and* `out.data["reviewer"]` is set, because — as the retained comment says — in that case "something else has printed": the review runner has already emitted its result (under `--json`, the one JSON body) and the command only returns `REFUSED` because the gate rejected it. The new second `if c.json and out.exit != OK` ignores that distinction and unconditionally calls `c.out(...)`. So for input `ddflow review --json <id>` where a real reviewer runs, produces findings, and the gate refuses (`out.exit == REFUSED`, `out.data["reviewer"]` truthy), stdout now carries two JSON documents: the runner's result body plus this synthetic `{"refusal": ..., "gate": ...}` object. Any consumer (and any test that does `json.loads(capsys...out)`) fails on the concatenated output, and the docstring's promise that stdout holds "the one body" is broken. The body should only be synthesized under the same condition used for the stderr message, i.e. `out.exit == FAIL or (out.exit in (NOTHING, REFUSED) and not out.data.get("reviewer"))`. The failing-test case in the task (no item, no reviewer) does hit the empty-output branch, so the regression test passes while this path regresses silently.

chunk_findings.detail:
The new branch classifies *every* covering job that is not in `done` as "unfinished, go wait for it". `pending` only filters on `isinstance(j, dict)`, `_covers(git_ref, sha)` and `_job_id(j) is not None` — there is no test that the job is still in a non-terminal state. So a job whose status is terminal-but-not-finished (e.g. `failed`, `error`, `canceled`) is taken as `j = max(pending, ...)` and the function returns, for input `{"id": 7, "git_ref": "<sha>", "status": "failed"}`:

`"roborev job 7 for <sha[:10]> is failed, not done: `roborev wait 7` first ...; the reviewer is unchecked"`

That message is self-contradictory ("is failed, not done") and, worse, its instruction is a dead end: `roborev wait 7` returns immediately because the job is already terminal, no review for the sha will ever be produced, and re-running the gate reproduces the identical message — the standards gate stays permanently unavailable, which is exactly the failure mode B08da521f70 set out to remove. The regression test only exercises `status="running"`, so this path is uncovered. Terminal non-done statuses should fall through to the "holds no finished review …; re-run `roborev review <sha>`" message, not be told to wait.

data.title: ddflow/services/roborev.py:85-97 (the new `pending` branch)

chunk_findings.detail: This is the only test in the new diff that exercises a terminal-but-not-`done` covering job, and it pins only two substrings: `"roborev wait"` must be absent and `"no finished review"` must be present.
